newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish one-day depos jump on reserve end, zloty up.
newsitem.headline: Polish one-day depos jump on reserve end, zloty up.

text.p: Polish one-day deposit rates jumped the lombard rate levels on Tuesday under upward pressure from banks which wanted to square reserve positions on the squeeze money market, dealers said.

They said bids nearly reached the 25 percent lombard rate when suppliers decided to sell cash surpluses to cash-hungry banks looking to balance required reserves before the end of October's period on Wednesday.
"Finally suppliers were satisfied with the price level started to sell, stopping the rate rally at the lombard's 25 percent," said Krzysztof Chmura from Bank Gdanski SA.
Overnight and tomorrow/next rates were quoted at 24.80/25.20 percent, up from Monday's 19.50/20.50 percent and 20.20/21.20 percent respectively.
Some dealers said Tusday's high price levels were caused by unexpected outflows from corporate clients this week.
They said that after a severe money shortage at the end of September banks were not likely to have left large gaps on required reserve levels this month.
"The cash shotage may have been caused by big client ouflows from Monday," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz from PKO BP.
Traders said high spot/next rates, at 19.00/21.00 percent may signal that one-day depos will stay at high levels for several days into the new reserve period.
"If S/N stays high, one-day rates may stay there even after the new reserve period starts," Wieczorkiewicz said.
The zloty closed at 1.91/1.86 percent from the trading band centre stronger than Monday's close at 1.86/1.81 percent after trailing the dollar's losses to the mark on world marekts.
It closed at 2.8091/01 per dollar, up from 2.8215/25 on Monday and at 1.8606/18 to the mark, down from 1.8522/35.
